videos.title: Snowplow that actually stops
videos.description: Wide wedge, weight centered, and looking where you want to go. First confidence drill on a gentle green.

notes.abstract: A snowplow that actually slows you down: wide wedge, centered weight, and eyes where you want to go.
points: Open a stable wedge with weight centered between both skis.
Look where you want to travel, not at the tips.
Press evenly to scrub speed before you try to turn.
notes.conclusion: If you are still accelerating, the wedge is too narrow or weight is in the back seat.

videos.title: Linking plow turns
videos.description: Tip the skis inside the wedge and move pressure from ski to ski without standing up tall.

notes.abstract: Linking plow turns by tipping inside the wedge and moving pressure ski to ski without standing tall.
points: Tip the inside edges of the wedge to start direction change.
Shift pressure from ski to ski without popping upright.
Keep the plow shape until the link feels rhythmic.
notes.conclusion: Standing up tall mid-link kills edge engagement — stay compact and tip.

videos.title: How to fall and get up on skis
videos.description: Sit down early, keep tips downhill when you stand, and avoid twisting the knees.

notes.abstract: Falling and getting up on skis: sit early, keep tips downhill when you stand, avoid knee twist.
points: Choose a controlled sit instead of a twisting catch.
Organize tips downhill before you push up.
Use poles for help without yanking the knees sideways.
notes.conclusion: Getting up well matters as much as falling well — tips downhill first.

videos.title: Parallel turns on blue runs
videos.description: Matching skis after the fall line, quiet upper body, and a clean pole plant rhythm.

notes.abstract: Parallel turns on blues once the plow is reliable: match skis and steer with the outside ski.
points: Start closing the plow gradually as confidence grows.
Lead with outside-ski pressure through the turn.
Keep poles quiet and timing simple on blue terrain.
notes.conclusion: If the inside ski leads, you are still in plow habits — emphasis outside ski.

videos.title: Carving arcs without the skid
videos.description: Higher edge angles and angulation once parallel is solid. Side-camera study tip included.

notes.abstract: Cleaner carved arcs: tip earlier and hold the edge so the ski tracks instead of skids.
points: Roll onto edge earlier in the turn.
Hold pressure through the belly of the arc.
Release smoothly into the next tip without a long flat phase.
notes.conclusion: A carve leaves a thin track; a wide smear means you are still skidding.

videos.title: Mogul line reading
videos.description: Absorb and extend, keep hands quiet, and pick a zipper line that matches your speed.

notes.abstract: Mogul line reading: pick a path early, absorb with the legs, and keep upper body calm.
points: Choose a line before you are on top of the first bump.
Absorb with ankles and knees; keep the torso quieter.
Use short turns that match the bump rhythm.
notes.conclusion: Moguls punish late decisions — look two bumps ahead, not at your tips.

videos.title: First powder floats on skis
videos.description: Wider stance, centered pressure, and longer turns so tips stay up in soft snow.

notes.abstract: First powder on skis: slightly aft balance, longer turns, and enough speed to float.
points: Ease weight slightly aft so tips stay alive.
Lengthen the turn; powder resists quick edge changes.
Keep enough speed to plane without diving the tips.
notes.conclusion: Submarining usually means too slow or too far forward — float first.

videos.title: Steep hop turns
videos.description: Commit to the fall line, hop to release edges, and land ready for the next turn.

notes.abstract: Steep hop turns for when a long carve is the wrong tool: quick unweight, land, and set.
points: Unweight both skis together to redirect in tight terrain.
Land and set the edges before the next hop.
Keep hops short and controlled above exposure.
notes.conclusion: Hop turns are survival tools — rhythm and commitment beat big swings.

videos.title: Tree skiing speed control
videos.description: Short turns, gap reading, and keeping eyes up through the next opening.

notes.abstract: Tree skiing speed control: pick gaps, shorten turns, and never enter without an exit.
points: Scan for gaps and an exit before you commit.
Use short turns to keep speed honest in tight spacing.
When trees densify, slow the cadence instead of forcing width.
notes.conclusion: In trees, line choice is the technique — speed without an exit is the danger.

videos.title: Race-inspired short turns
videos.description: Early edge, strong outside ski, and a compact pole plant for groomer performance.

notes.abstract: Race-inspired short turns: quick edge changes, strong outside ski, compact upper body.
points: Snap to the new edge early and often.
Drive the outside ski while the inside ski stays light.
Keep the upper body calm so the legs can work fast.
notes.conclusion: Short turns are timing, not muscle — edge early, release clean, repeat.

resorts.name: Val d'Isère
resorts.summary: High-altitude grooming, glacier access, and serious alpine terrain.
resorts.intro:
Val d'Isère suits skiers who want reliable snow and long linked valleys.

Beginner areas exist, but the mountain's personality is intermediate-to-advanced.

Pricing sits in the not-cheap range, especially in peak holiday weeks.

resorts.name: St. Anton
resorts.summary: Legendary off-piste culture with lively village energy.
resorts.intro:
St. Anton is a classic introduction to alpine off-piste mindset.

Trees and itineraries reward confident parallel skiers. Hire local knowledge if you leave the marked world.

Expect premium pricing and strong après.

resorts.name: Niseko
resorts.summary: Powder benchmark with night skiing and tree runs.
resorts.intro:
Niseko works beautifully for skiers chasing soft snow and floodlit evenings.

Tree skiing is a highlight after storms. Peak season lodging is expensive near Hirafu.

resorts.name: Formigal-Panticosa
resorts.summary: Broad terrain with often friendlier pricing than the big Alpine hubs.
resorts.intro:
A solid option when you want variety without Swiss or French peak prices.

Good intermediate grooming and family-friendly zones; advanced lines appear when the snowpack cooperates.
